why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open water and the marinas and piers already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 sold out), decarbonization mandates turned diesel fleets into liabilities, and the hybrid removed the range excuse. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Bolt's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Bolt brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Bolt's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Bolt — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

markets.summary: Cyprus pairs a year-round Mediterranean climate with three resort poles — Ayia Napa/Protaras, Larnaca and Limassol/Paphos — strung along a coast where the road network forces long inland detours between beaches that sit minutes apart by water. Bolt is already a leading ridehail brand on the island; a foiling water tier turns the airport-to-resort and resort-to-resort transfers into the fastest, cleanest leg of the trip.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Cyprus, the sun-coast water shuttle

hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Cyprus's three resort clusters — airport-to-resort hops, beach-to-beach shuttles, and a Quanta-LR regional spine linking Limassol and Larnaca, with a roadmap leg across to Lebanon.

markets.why_now: Cyprus draws ~4M visitors a year against a population of ~0.9M, heavily concentrated in summer along a thin coastal strip. The Ayia Napa–Protaras and Larnaca–Ayia Napa roads choke every July; the water beside them is empty and flat. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the dense southern-coast hops today.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet: a Bolt car from the terminal to the marina, a foiling hop to the resort, a Bolt scooter for the last 300m. Cyprus is small enough that a single multimodal chain can own the entire arrival journey.
markets.partner_context: Bolt operates ridehail across Cyprus and has deep brand trust with both residents and the large tourist inflow. Marine adds a premium, weather-resilient tier on exactly the corridors where summer road congestion is worst — without Bolt touching a hull.
markets.why_navier_now: Pioneer II (8 pax, commercial now) covers the ≤70nm southern-coast and airport-resort legs immediately. The Limassol–Larnaca regional run (35nm) is comfortably in Pioneer range; the Larnaca–Beirut crossing (115nm) is explicitly a Quanta-LR roadmap leg, never faked on a 70nm boat.
markets.differentiation: Against the airport taxi: comparable door-to-door cost at a fraction of the time in peak season, zero local emissions, and a view. Against the diesel excursion boat: quiet, foiling, on-demand and in-app rather than fixed-departure.

proof_points.claim: The resort poles are minutes apart by water but long by road.

objections.concern: Three separate clusters dilute density.
objections.response: We anchor one cluster (Ayia Napa) first to prove unit economics, then replicate the proven playbook to Larnaca and Limassol rather than spreading thin from day one.

markets.close: Cyprus is a compact, year-round, tourism-dense island where the road is the bottleneck and the water is the shortcut — an ideal proving ground for a Bolt-branded foiling tier.

markets.label: Egypt — Cairo & Red Sea
markets.summary: Egypt pairs two distinct, dense water markets: the Red Sea resort coast (Hurghada, El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh, Sharm El Sheikh) where reef-and-resort hops are the core leisure economy, and the Nile through Greater Cairo, a 20-million-person city split by a river it barely uses for transport. Bolt is a leading ride-hail brand in Egypt; the water tier monetises both.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — Egypt, Red Sea reefs and the Cairo Nile
hero.subtitle: Fly the reef hops and the river commute, in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded foiling water tier on the Red Sea resort coast and the Cairo Nile — all-electric reef-and-resort hops and a flying river link across Greater Cairo.

markets.why_now: Egypt is targeting 30M tourists, with the Red Sea its fastest-growing coast and a new wave of resort and marina development at El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh and the Red Sea Riviera. Meanwhile Greater Cairo's road congestion is among the worst on earth and the Nile is wide, calm and almost unused for transport. Both are textbook foiling corridors.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app, same wallet: a Bolt car to the marina or corniche pier, a foiling Pioneer II across the reef or the river, a Bolt car on arrival.
markets.partner_context: Bolt operates ride-hail at scale across Egyptian cities including Cairo. Egypt is a high-trip, price-sensitive market where the water leg adds a premium tier without new app behaviour.
markets.why_navier_now: Every core Red Sea and Cairo corridor is ≤16nm — squarely Pioneer II, commercial today. The piers exist: El Gouna's lagoon network, Hurghada Marina, Sharm's jetties, and the Cairo corniche. No regional Quanta-LR leg is needed to start.
markets.differentiation: Against the diesel excursion boat: faster to the reefs, no fumes over protected coral, and bookable on demand. Against the Cairo road: a flying river crossing that sidesteps the bridges entirely.

proof_points.claim: The Red Sea is Egypt's fastest-growing tourism coast.
proof_points.evidence: Hurghada, El Gouna, Sahl Hasheesh and Sharm El Sheikh anchor a dense reef-and-resort water economy with constant short hops.

proof_points.claim: El Gouna is a purpose-built lagoon town.
proof_points.evidence: Its internal lagoon network already moves people by boat — an ideal all-electric foiling showcase.

proof_points.claim: The Cairo Nile is an unused transport artery.
proof_points.evidence: Greater Cairo's ~20M people are split by a wide, calm river with minimal scheduled water transport despite extreme road congestion.

proof_points.claim: Bolt already owns the rider in Egypt.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt runs ride-hail across Egyptian cities; the water leg slots into an existing app.

objections.concern: Egypt is price-sensitive — will riders pay a water premium?
objections.response: On the Red Sea the comparison is a paid excursion boat, which the foiling hop beats on time and experience at a comparable fare; in Cairo the premium buys a guaranteed time saving across an otherwise gridlocked city.

objections.concern: Reef zones are environmentally protected.
objections.response: That favours us — an electric, no-wake foiler is far gentler on coral than a diesel excursion fleet, and aligns with Red Sea conservation rules.

objections.concern: Nile permitting is complex.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a natural water-transport city.
proof_points.evidence: The city spans 14 islands with an established commuter-ferry culture and a 30,000-island archipelago beyond.

proof_points.claim: The city is electrifying its waterborne transport.
proof_points.evidence: Stockholm has active programmes to decarbonise its ferries and meet climate-neutral targets — directly favouring an electric foiler.

proof_points.claim: The quays already exist.
proof_points.evidence: Slussen, Nybroplan, Strömkajen, Stadshuskajen and Djurgården are working passenger quays — Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal.

proof_points.claim: Stockholm is a flagship Bolt market in Bolt's home region.
proof_points.evidence: Bolt operates ride-hail and micromobility across the Nordics/Baltics from its Estonian base.

objections.concern: Stockholm winters ice over.
objections.response: The Prove fleet is sized to the open-water season; the foiling hull's all-electric, all-weather operating envelope is validated on the warmer Med and Gulf legs first, with winter operating limits set conservatively.

objections.concern: The city already runs commuter ferries.
objections.response: On diesel, on fixed timetables, with no app booking. The foiling tier wins on speed, emissions and on-demand convenience, and complements rather than replaces the trunk ferry routes.

objections.concern: Is there enough premium demand?
objections.response: Central hops compete on time saved against a congested island core, and the archipelago leisure runs (Vaxholm, Drottningholm) carry a clear leisure premium.

markets.the_ask: Co-brand a Stockholm water tier with Bolt, launching a 2-boat Prove fleet on the central inner-city hops in 2026 H2, scaling into the inner archipelago as quay agreements land.
markets.close: Stockholm is a water city that forgot to fly. Bolt owns the home-region rider; Navier brings the boat. Let's put the archipelago in the app.
markets.end_state: A foiling inner-Stockholm and inner-archipelago network in the Bolt app, with Quanta-LR opening the Åland crossing.

markets.label: UAE — Dubai & Abu Dhabi
markets.summary: The UAE is the anchor market: Dubai's jetty-dense waterfront (Palm, Dubai Harbour, Bluewaters, La Mer) plus the Dubai–Abu Dhabi corridor form the densest premium water-mobility opportunity in the network. Bolt's regional ambition meets a market already conditioned to on-demand luxury transfers.

hero.title: Bolt × Navier — UAE, the anchor market
hero.subtitle: Foil between Dubai's jetties and on to Abu Dhabi, booked in the Bolt app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Bolt-branded electric-foiling tier across Dubai's jetty network, scaling to a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor — the flagship of the Bolt water network.

markets.why_now: Dubai has the world's densest cluster of luxury hotel and residence jetties, a government actively promoting marine transport, and a clientele that already pays for premium transfers. The Dubai–Abu Dhabi road is a 90-minute-plus drive the water can shortcut. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears every intra-Dubai jetty hop.
markets.multimodal_fit: Same Bolt app and wallet: a Bolt car to the jetty, a foiling hop between Palm resorts or across to Abu Dhabi, seamless return — a single premium chain on the corridors where road congestion and heat make driving least attractive.
markets.partner_context: Bolt is expanding its regional premium ambitions. The UAE is where a co-branded marine tier has the highest willingness-to-pay and the strongest government tailwind — the natural anchor to prove the model before replicating it across the network.
markets.why_navier_now: Every intra-Dubai jetty leg (0.5–1.2nm) is trivially inside Pioneer II range. The Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche corridor (55.8nm) sits inside the 70nm Pioneer envelope — a genuine near-term regional run, not a roadmap aspiration.
markets.differentiation: Against the chauffeur car: comparable cost, far faster jetty-to-jetty, air-conditioned cabin and a skyline view with zero local emissions. Against the diesel water taxi: foiling-quiet, on-demand and in-app.

proof_points.claim: Dubai has the densest luxury-jetty network in the world.
proof_points.evidence: Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Harbour, Bluewaters and La Mer concentrate dozens of premium jetties within 1–2nm of each other.

proof_points.claim: Dubai–Abu Dhabi is a Pioneer-range regional corridor.
proof_points.evidence: Dubai Marina–Abu Dhabi Corniche is ~56nm, inside Pioneer II's 70nm envelope.

proof_points.claim: Government actively promotes marine mobility.
proof_points.evidence: Dubai's marine-transport agenda and abundant licensed marina infrastructure support a water tier.

proof_points.claim: High willingness-to-pay for premium transfers.
proof_points.evidence: An established luxury on-demand transfer market gives the strongest unit economics in the network.

objections.concern: Summer heat limits demand.
objections.response: Air-conditioned foiling cabins make water transfer more comfortable than open-deck alternatives, and premium indoor-to-indoor jetty transfers are most attractive precisely when it's hottest.

objections.concern: Dubai already has water taxis.
objections.response: We add a premium, foiling, all-electric on-demand tier in the Bolt app — faster and quieter than the existing diesel water taxis, not a like-for-like substitute.

objections.concern: Abu Dhabi is far by water.
objections.response: At 56nm it's inside Pioneer II range — a genuine Phase-3 regional corridor, not a faked long leg.

markets.the_ask: Make the UAE the Bolt water flagship — a 3-boat Pioneer II anchor across Dubai's jetty network, scaling to 8 boats and a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor.
markets.close: The UAE is the highest-value, highest-readiness water-mobility market on earth — the natural anchor to prove Bolt-on-water before the network replicates it.
markets.end_state: A dense Dubai jetty network plus a Dubai–Abu Dhabi regional corridor, the flagship of the Bolt water network.
